name: Haiku contrarian turnarounds
strategy: Contrarian recovery book holding beaten-down AI-disrupted SaaS (ADBE, CRM, SQ) and deeply drawn-down crypto (BTC, ETH) at unchanged weights, with 16% cash and new stop-losses added to cap further downside.
reassessment_note: The 2H rebound thesis has not yet shown up in the tape: software stocks kept falling on 11-17 (CRM -9.5% with no company news, 57 of 62 large application-software peers down that day) and BTC fell with risk assets on 11-20. I am not adding exposure into that. I am also not cutting into the selloff, because I found no company-specific break in ADBE, CRM, SQ, BTC or ETH and selling after a sector-wide drop locks in losses. Instead I keep the existing weights and attach stops so that a further leg down exits the position rather than compounding the -23% drawdown. I dropped MSTR, which carried 0% weight and was dead weight in the packet. Research was limited to a handful of searches, and some results were undated or from prior years, so I am treating the packet marks as the authority.

positions.thesis: Adobe is trading near multi-year lows after a long de-rating on AI-disruption fears from newer, smaller competitors, and I have no company-specific news showing its franchise has broken. Holding at 25% keeps the rebound option, with a 25% stop from the 11-23 entry to cap a further leg down.

Salesforce fell 9.5% on 11-17 with no company announcement while 57 of 62 peers also fell, so the move looks sector-driven rather than company-specific. The position stays at 25% as the largest contrarian bet, with a 25% stop because the sector trend is still negative.
Block is a fintech that has fallen with the broader growth and fintech complex; the position stays at a smaller 13% weight, with a 25% stop to limit the downside of a continued fintech drawdown.

BTC fell about 5% on 11-20 with risk assets and is well below the entry fill, but the drawdown is consistent with a deep crypto cycle low rather than a broken thesis. I keep 12% with a 20% stop because the 11-20 selloff showed risk-off correlation and a further break would argue for exit.

ETH is down more than BTC in the packet and tracks the same risk-off tape, so I hold at 9% rather than add. The 25% stop is wider than BTC's because ETH already sits deeper in its drawdown, and I want to avoid being shaken out on a retest of lows.
